correctness.rationale: The character and Haar normalizations are reconstructed explicitly. Exact differentiation yields B_L=-N cos(2Ntheta)+(cot theta/2)sin(2Ntheta). Exact removal of spin L-1 gives main angular multiplier -(2cos(2theta)-1)N cos(2Ltheta), with O(log N) remainder in L1. The bounded-variation absolute-cosine averaging lemma and exact |2cos(2theta)-1| integral pi/3+2sqrt(3) prove both sharp asymptotic constants for every integer L tending to infinity. Finite symbolic and quadrature checks corroborate, but cannot replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2020 compact Lie group harmonic-analysis literature establishes irreducible character and eigenfunction restriction estimates, not the one-hole Peter–Weyl endpoint comparison. The 1986 general Lebesgue-constant full-text theorem establishes growth orders for complete cutoffs. The closest published exact SU(2) theorem treats every highest weight, not SO(3) even weights with the penultimate spin deleted. The exact trig polynomial profile and norm inflation factor are not corollaries of their stated claims. Search is not proof of priority; one plausible 1988 specialist article remains inaccessible.

value.rationale: Spectral Lebesgue constants quantify sharp endpoint amplification of rotation-group Fourier approximations. The explicit ratio 1/3+2sqrt(3)/pi>1 shows a substantial strict degradation from omitting only one adjacent-high-spin irreducible sector. This motivates spectral-mask design; the all-spin leading constant and complete exact one-hole ratio are a natural nontrivial invariant, not a routine numerical finite slice.
